clue.text: Were a couple of hours fairly employed in school?

indicators.note: something employed in a place works inside it, so these letters go inside the school

parts.note: a coed is a mixed school, taking both sexes
a bit means fairly or somewhat, as in a bit tired

explanation.surface: A question about whether a few hours were well spent at school.
explanation.walkthrough: A coed is a co-educational school, chiefly an American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to live together as partners without being married, so it describes having been a couple.

clue.text: Sound of one planting tree

indicators.note: sound of tells us to find a word that sounds like the phrase that follows

parts.note: a seeder is someone or something that plants seed

explanation.surface: The sound a gardener makes setting a tree in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedar is a large coniferous evergreen, such as the cedar of Lebanon.

clue.text: Whiff of something unpleasant in impetuous senior pupil

indicators.note: the smell goes in the adjective for impetuous

parts.note: heady means rash, impetuous
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A rash sixth-former leaves an unpleasant smell.
explanation.walkthrough: A head boy is the senior pupil chosen to represent a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the head boy is a leading pupil appointed as a representative and role model.

clue.text: Part of treatment for Jack's brother to have daily

parts.note: Br is the abbreviation for brother, as for a monk
to own is to have
a daily is a newspaper

explanation.surface: A boy named Jack has a brother who takes a daily newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill, Jack went to bed 'to mend his head with vinegar and brown paper'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme names vinegar and brown paper as the remedy for Jack's broken crown.

clue.text: Workers organised party on river for Mary?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the party comes before the river

parts.note: a TU, a trade union, is workers organised together
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Union workers plan a riverside party for someone called Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary I of England was a Tudor monarch, so Mary is one example of the dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Mary I, daughter of Henry VIII, belonged to the royal house that ruled England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Trouble leading to arrest: ring for the minister!

indicators.note: the trouble comes first, leading on to the arrest

parts.note: to dog is to trouble or plague
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Trouble ends in an arrest, so someone shouts to phone the minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it is the circular collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman wears a stiff white band around the neck, worn by ministers of religion.

clue.text: Firm support for committee in crisis?

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Asks what solid backing a crisis committee can rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA is the UK government's emergency committee, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A where it meets.
explanation.definitionFit: The British government convenes this emergency body whenever a national crisis breaks.

clue.text: Copper, officer who inspires devotion?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Lt is a lieutenant

explanation.surface: Asks whether a police officer inspires loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A cult is the excessive veneration of a person or thing, a form of devotion.

clue.text: Young Italian graduate doctor with two November visits

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

indicators.note: the November letter visits, going inside the pair of ones

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newly qualified doctor makes two visits in November.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambini is Italian for babies or small children, the Italian young.

clue.text: Beholds an unusually fair lady

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters take an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices a remarkably beautiful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as beautiful, but here it means light-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash blonde is a woman with pale, greyish fair hair.

clue.text: Odd man out: one must enter playing field

indicators.note: the numeral is required to go inside the rearranged letters
out describes something disordered or not right, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about spotting the odd man out once someone steps onto the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd man out' looks like a set phrase but splits into fodder and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseball field is called a diamond from the shape formed by its four bases.

clue.text: Proceed clumsily — you fall behind, reversing at speed

indicators.note: reversing tells us the letters for you and fall behind are read backwards together

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
to lag is to fall behind
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A clumsy runner lags behind, then backs up at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll coined the word for moving in a heavy, lumbering, ungainly way.

clue.text: Hood for one to prepare in vestry

parts.note: Robin Hood, the outlaw, is one example of a Hood
to groom is to prepare or get ready, as a candidate is groomed

explanation.surface: An actor playing Robin Hood gets ready in a church vestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood for one' points to the outlaw's first name, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is the room where clergy put on their robes before a service.

clue.text: Finally, feeling poorly, you get a breather

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell, you are told to take a short break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest, but here it means an organ for breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish's gill is its respiratory organ, so in a literal sense it is a breathing device.

clue.text: Being flameproof, vests ultimately a hit with US hospital department

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of vests

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to lam is to hit hard
and means with, together with
ER, emergency room, is the American casualty department

explanation.surface: Fireproof vests become a big hit in an American emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the salamander is a creature that can live in fire unharmed.

clue.text: Groups tramp through my local area last of all

indicators.note: the last letter of all the words in the phrase are taken

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bands of people trudge through the speaker's neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a phylum is a major taxonomic group, ranking below kingdom; the plural is phyla.

clue.text: Some chicken leg remains from a classic order

parts.note: part means some, a portion
a hen is a chicken
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Leftover chicken leg from a takeaway order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Parthenon in Athens is the great ruined temple built in the Doric order of classical architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruined Athenian temple to Athena is built in the Doric style, one of the classical orders.

clue.text: Ruse native maybe's done in lab with airgun

indicators.note: done in means wrecked, so the letters are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trickster dispatched in a laboratory with an airgun.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruse is a city in Bulgaria on the Danube; the capital letter hides it behind the everyday word for a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in the Bulgarian city of Ruse is an example of a person from that country.

clue.text: Serving in household, however large, royal home included

parts.note: but means however

indicators.note: the royal and home letters are included within the abbreviation for large

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty
in means at home

explanation.surface: Service in any household, however grand, even a royal palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Butlering is working as a butler, the head manservant of a household.

clue.text: The city of Charlotte located east of Fairfax?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a city in Kent, and also one in New York State

definitions.text: of Charlotte located east of Fairfax?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Charlotte Brontë's hero in Jane Eyre is Edward Fairfax ..., so his surname comes after Fairfax

explanation.surface: Seems to place the city of Charlotte, North Carolina, east of Fairfax, Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry, east is to the right, so a name located east of Fairfax follows it in the full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë named Jane Eyre's employer and love Edward Fairfax Rochester, and Rochester is also a Kentish cathedral town.

clue.text: Row after whip becomes more spiteful

indicators.note: the row comes after the whip

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip, called the cat
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel after a whipping turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it means a line or level.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty means spiteful and sly, so its comparative means nastier.

clue.text: Passage one's going to broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so we want a word sounding like the phrase

parts.note: I'll, short for I will, says that one is going to do something

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are about to go on air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or plane.

clue.text: Mountain transport being cut back interrupts take-off

indicators.note: the shortened word breaks into the parody

parts.note: a skit is a parody, a take-off

indicators.note: cut back means the word is cut short at its back end

parts.note: being means existence, life

explanation.surface: Uphill transport, cut back, gets in the way of a plane's take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-off' looks like flight, but it means an imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift carries skiers up a mountain on chairs or tows.

clue.text: Strikes clues: a certain number removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away from the word for clues

parts.note: hints are clues
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's strike: some of the clues have been withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits as a verb means strikes, as when someone hits or strikes a ball.

clue.text: Getting one's fair share to eat, after clinching English league

indicators.note: to clinch is to grasp tightly, so the pair of words holds the letter between them
the fair share comes after the word for having eaten

parts.note: fed means given something to eat
a ration is a fixed allowance, one's fair share

explanation.surface: Someone gets a fair portion of food after a deal is clinched with England.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting one's fair share to eat suggests being fed one's ration.
explanation.definitionFit: A federation is a union of states or bodies, so it is an alliance or league.

clue.text: Old king hoarded wine bottles

indicators.note: bottles means contains, so the answer is held within these words

parts.note: the letters run on across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An ancient king stockpiled wine in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin was a seventh-century king of Northumbria, an Anglo-Saxon monarch.

clue.text: State name, number after one is hauled up

indicators.note: the reversed number comes after the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue hauled up means the letters run upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a reg, registration number, is a car's number plate

explanation.surface: A name is called out and a numbered person is dragged up.
explanation.walkthrough: A reg is a vehicle's registration number in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a country in West Africa, an independent nation state.

clue.text: A duck or ducks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a score of zero
second meaning: a term of endearment

explanation.walkthrough: Ducks is a northern English endearment, much like love.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means nothing in tennis scoring and is also a familiar endearment like ducks.

clue.text: Capital made of one "very naughty boy" holding nothing back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read from end to start

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the boy's name contains the zero

parts.note: from Monty Python's Life of Brian: he's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A city built from a mischievous boy who keeps nothing in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Brian's mother's line in Monty Python's Life of Brian.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Our team had row before golf match

indicators.note: before places the din ahead of the golf letter

parts.note: we is the team that includes the speaker
'd is the contracted form of had, as in we'd
a din is a noisy row
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Our side squabbled ahead of a golf match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting fixture from the golf, but it means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage or union, as in a good match, so a wedding fits.

clue.text: Enquiry's led with nothing odd in mind

indicators.note: with nothing odd in the odd places, only the even letters are kept

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An inquiry headed by someone with nothing strange on their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Enquiry's is ignored, as punctuation usually is.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind a patient or child is to look after them, which is what it means to nurse.

clue.text: Source of power in the Information Age at peak

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
an era is an age
a tor is a rocky peak, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Asks where power comes from in the Information Age at its height.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator produces electricity, so it is a source of power.
